newsitem.title: UK: SiemensPlessey surprised by UK contract end.
newsitem.headline: SiemensPlessey surprised by UK contract end.

text.p: Siemens AG's Siemens Plessey Systems on Tuesday expressed surprise at the decision of Britain's Defence Ministry to terminate a 50 million stg deal with it, saying it had fully met the contract specifications on time.
"The Ministry recognises that we do not accept its grounds for termination and arbitration procedures have now been initiated," the company said in a statement.

Defence Procurement Minister James Arbuthnot said on Monday the ministry would consider pursuing a claim for compensation from Siemens Plessey after tests carried out last year and in 1995 showed its VIXEN system had "operational shortcomings."
But the Siemens Plessey statement said: "The company delivered the core VIXEN system, fully meeting the contracted specification within the agreed timescales."
"Deliveries against the contract took place in late 1994/early 1995, and VIXEN could have been taken into operation service at the end of 1995."

The company said it recognised the threat against which VIXEN was designed had changed significantly since the contract was awarded and understood the ministry may now be looking for a simpler system.
"However, the VIXEN requirement was endorsed by the Ministry of Defence in 1994 and all contracted trials have been successfully completed," it said.
The Vixen system was designed to collect and disseminate accurate signals intelligence from a high density, dynamic electronic environment.
